metadata.title: the dijker | move yourself
metadata.description: The dijker is a four-wheeled vehicle you drive with your legs. You brake by pushing the steering wheel and shift gears with your toes, through the spiral belt drive multispeed®.

hero.title: the dijker
hero.lead: The dijker looks like it has been on the road for decades. Yet nothing like it existed before.
hero.sub: Under that classic shape sits new engineering. The dijker runs on the spiral belt drive multispeed®, a drive no other vehicle has.

dijker.heading: Highlights at a glance
dijker.intro: Five things that set the dijker apart.
dijker.body1: The dijker has four wheels and a small steering wheel. To brake, you push that steering wheel in. The pedals move back and forth in a straight line, left and right independently. The body comes in two parts: an open luggage compartment, the boot, and a nose cover. Both come off in seconds.
dijker.body2: There are no brake levers. There are no gear levers either, because you shift by moving your toes backwards. It rides like nothing you have tried before, and it is a lot of fun.

comfort.title: comfort
comfort.text: Made for commuters who now take the car, a motorbike or public transport. You sit leaning back and stay dry, so you arrive rested. With the nose cover on there is still plenty of airflow, and you can hang your jacket over the open-fabric backrest.

protection.title: protection
protection.text: Four sturdy wheels and a strong chassis keep you safe on the road. A small poncho between the boot and the nose cover keeps out cold and rain. A brightly coloured flag makes sure other traffic sees you.

fast.title: fast
fast.text: You push with both legs at once and the dijker weighs very little. That gives you a quick start from standstill, and at speed the streamlined shape helps.

free.title: free
free.text: The dijker is open, so getting in and out is easy. You are never shut in.

boot.title: boot
boot.text: At the back is one large luggage compartment with no dividers, the boot. It comes off as easily as the nose cover.

technique.heading: The technique
technique.chassis: Everything is mounted on the chassis, a flat plate. It holds the suspension, steering rack, pedal guides and brake distribution. The brake cables, wiring and drive belts run through it, out of harm's way. The chassis is strong and light.
technique.drive: Drive and gearing are one system. Each belt winds around the wheel axle in a spiral. While you push, belt length is added or taken away, which makes the diameter bigger or smaller. You can even shift down while standing still. A bicycle derailleur can't do that.
technique.brakes: All four wheels have light-alloy drum brakes. You brake by pushing the steering wheel in, and the steering column passes that movement on. It sounds odd, but in practice it comes naturally.

creator.heading: The inventor
creator.name: Peter-Paul van der Ven
creator.body1: Peter-Paul knows physics, materials and tribology. He designs and tests sandwich structures and linear pedal mechanisms.
creator.body2: The dijker is a childhood dream come true. As a boy he saw the air around us getting dirtier. He wanted to build small vehicles with little or no exhaust, vehicles he would want to ride himself. The goal is that car owners will pick one too.

investing.heading: Investing
investing.body: The dijker works. The next step is further development and bringing it to market. Want to invest, or take on a major role in the project? Get in touch.
